## Overview

Immigrant visas to the United States are processed for citizens and residents of Bangladesh at the U.S. Embassy in Dhaka.

To apply for an immigrant visa, a foreign citizen seeking to immigrate generally must be sponsored by a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident immediate relative(s), or prospective U.S. employer, and have an approved petition before applying for an immigrant visa.  The sponsor begins the process by filing a petition on the foreign citizen’s behalf with U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS).  You may wish to review our [Directory of Visa Categories](https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/us-visas.html) on usvisas.state.gov to learn about the different types of immigrant visas to the United States.  Then, follow the steps on the [Immigrant Visa Process](https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/us-visas/immigrate/the-immigrant-visa-process.html) on usvisas.state.gov to begin applying for an immigrant visa.

Once USCIS has approved your petition and you have completed pre-processing with the National Visa Center (NVC), review the instructions given to you by the NVC, along with the information presented on this website, for further guidance and instructions.

## Important Notice About Immigrant Visa Processing

Effective June 01, 2026, U.S. Embassy, Dhaka has implemented two-day processing for all immigrant visa categories.  Visit our [***Directory of Visa Categories***](https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/us-visas/visa-information-resources/all-visa-categories.html "https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/us-visas/visa-information-resources/all-visa-categories.html") and check the Immigrant Visa Categories for more information.

The applicants must visit the embassy at least **twice **during the immigrant visa process. For the first visit, they should go to the scheduled appointment made by the National Visa Center (NVC).

- - - Bring **all your original required documents** and copies.
    - Before the appointment, make sure you have uploaded all the required documents to your [CEAC](https://ceac.state.gov/IV/Login.aspx) account. If any are missing, you must upload them.
    - During this first visit, we will review your documents, collect fingerprints and photos, and decide whether the document review is complete.

**No Missing Documents**

**If there are no missing documents**, the review is complete. We will give you an appointment letter that tells you the date and time for the **immigrant visa interview** (The second appointment). Usually, it will be the same week as the document review.

- - - The Embassy will keep all the original documents, **except for your passport**. You **must** bring it to the interview.
    - You must return to the U.S. Embassy, Dhaka, on the scheduled date and time for the second visa appointment with a consular officer.

**Missing Documents**

**If there are missing documents**, we will give you a letter that lists the documents that are missing. It will have instructions for rescheduling your second interview with a consular officer.

- - Once you get the missing documents **and** upload them to your [CEAC](https://ceac.state.gov/IV/Login.aspx) account, reschedule the appointment using the [online profile](https://www.usvisascheduling.com/en-US/).
  - Bring all the original documents, including those listed on the letter, to the interview.

## Current Priority Date

**A Note Regarding Visa Availability  **

The issuance of family sponsored and employment based preference visas are numerically limited by congress. Interviews for applicants in these categories are scheduled when the applicant’s priority date becomes current and visa numbers are available. However, priority dates may change, and it is possible that at the time of the interview, visa numbers may no longer be available. If visa numbers are no longer available for your visa category, your interview will proceed as scheduled, but your visa not be issued until the priority date again becomes current and new numbers are available. Applicants should check the Visa Bulletin on the Department of State’s website for up to date information on priority dates for all immigrant visa categories.  

**CURRENT PRIORITY DATES  **

[Learn more about your priority date](https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/legal/visa-law0/visa-bulletin.html).

### Dates for November 2026

**F1:** 22 JAN 2021 (Unmarried Sons / Daughters of U.S. Citizens)

**F2A:** 22 OCT 2026 (Spouse and under 21 children of Legal Permanent Residents)

**FX:** 22 APR 2026 (F2A Cases with older priority dates)

**F2B:** 22 AUG 2020 (Unmarried Sons/Daughters of Legal Permanent Residents)

**F3:** 22 OCT 2015 (Married Sons/Daughters of U.S. Citizens)

**F4:** 22 OCT 2012 (Brothers/Sisters of U.S. Citizens and their Spouses & under 21 Children)

**E3:** 15 JUN 2024 (Skilled workers)

**EW:** 01 JUN 2022 (Un-Skilled Workers, their Spouse & Children)

## Fees

###### Immigrant Visas

- [Immediate relative and family preference applications](https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/us-visas/visa-information-resources/fees/fees-visa-services.html#permanent) (processed on the basis of an approved I-130, I-600 or I-800 petition): \$325
- [Employment-based applications ](http://www.travel.state.gov/content/visas/en/immigrate/employment.html)(processed on the basis of an approved I-140 petition) : \$345
- Other immigrant visa applications (including approved I-360 self-petitioners, special immigrant visa applicants, returning resident (SB-1) applicants, and all others, except DV program selectees): \$205
- [Orphan (intercountry adoption)](https://www.uscis.gov/i-600a) immediate relative petition (I-600, I-800): \$920
- Affidavit of Support Review (only when reviewed domestically): \$120

###### 

###### Other Fees

- Application for Determining Returning Resident Status, [Form DS-117](https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/us-visas/visa-information-resources/forms.html): \$180
- DHS Biometrics Fee: \$30

## Visa Inquiries

**Email:**

- [Support-bangladesh@usvisascheduling.com](mailto:support-bangladesh@usvisascheduling.com) (for all immigrant visa inquiries)
- <DhakaFraud@state.gov>; <fraud@ustraveldocs.com> (for visa fraud or malfeasance)

**Phone:**

- Callers in Bangladesh:Call [+88-09610202040](tel:+880%209610-202040)
- Callers in the United States:Call [+1-7039883466](tel:(703)%20988-3466)

**No inquiries will be accepted by fax or letter mail;**

Documents mailed to us through Bangladesh mail will be shredded upon receipt;

Documents mailed to us through international mail will be abandoned at Bangladesh Customs; we are unable to pay any fees to retrieve them.  Any personal identifiable information contained in such documents will be abandoned at the sender’s own risk.
